operators.name: avgpool1d_forward
semantics: Corresponds to reference statement x = self.pool(x) where self.pool is nn.AvgPool1d(kernel_size=3, stride=1, padding=1)
Performs 1D average pooling over the last dimension (length) for each batch and channel independently

Output length = floor((input_length + 2*padding - kernel_size) / stride) + 1. For the given input shape [512,3,50000], kernel_size=3, stride=1, padding=1, output length = floor((50000 + 2 - 3)/1) + 1 = 50000

Pooling window sums values in the range [i*stride - padding, i*stride - padding + kernel_size - 1], clamping indices at boundaries (implicit padding with zeros), then divides by count of valid (non-padded) elements
No bias, no activation, no batch normalization
Works elementwise identically to torch.nn.functional.avg_pool1d(input, kernel_size=3, stride=1, padding=1, ceil_mode=False, count_include_pad=True)

For this configuration count_include_pad defaults to True, meaning padded zeros are included in the average denominator when windows overlap padding, but since padding=1 and kernel=3, windows at boundaries have two valid elements and one padded zero, so denominator is 3 (count_include_pad=True) for all windows except possibly first and last? Actually with count_include_pad=True denominator is always kernel_size, regardless of padding. So output[i] = sum(valid window values) / kernel_size
Assumes input is contiguous or can be accessed with given strides; the custom op should handle arbitrary strides by reading via strides
Applies AvgPool1d(kernel_size=3, stride=1, padding=1) to input tensor x of shape [512,3,50000], float32, originally on CPU but expected to be moved to CUDA before call
Output tensor y has shape [512,3,50000], dtype float32, device cuda:0
For each batch b, channel c, output index i, y[b,c,i] = (sum_{j=max(0, i*1-1)}^{min(L-1, i*1-1+3-1)} x[b,c,j]) / 3, where L=50000 and padding zero outside
Returns the same tensor produced by step_001, no additional computation
